  │ read visible │ 1.68ms │ 0.53ms │
  └──────────────┴────────┴────────┘

  Both reads are well inside the poll budget, so the feed can keep reading every pane on each tick. The visible read is the one the notifier relies on,
  and it stays under two milliseconds even on a full 158-column pane with a long scrollback behind it, which leaves the rest of the five-second tick for
  the snapshot and the push check.

  One thing changed from the plan: the second read on a short answer is gone. Every read in the trace came back whole, and a retry that never fires is only
  a place for a bug to hide. If a short read ever shows up, the retry belongs in one function behind the transport, so putting it back is a small change
  that touches no caller.

  Two claims I checked on the wire myself: herdr reports interactive_ready on every pane it has started, so the write precondition can rely on it, and a
  closed pane's id comes back on the next new pane, so every write stays keyed on the agent's session rather than on the pane.

  What happens next

  Run the pane reads against the capture corpus → rerun the gate (ruff, basedpyright, complexipy, pytest) → read the geometry shots at 320px → fix what
  fails → commit. The background agents below are each reading one area and will report what they find.

  Nothing here needs root and nothing touches a live session: every check runs against the throwaway hp-test session or against the fixtures, so the
  agents in the default session are never read or written.

  I'll report once the background agents are back, with anything that changes the plan above, and leave the judgement calls about the feed's ordering to
  you when we get there.
